answer: Cross-cohort countersigning is a concrete sybil anchor: a new identity earns weight only when peers from three unrelated cohorts vouch for it, and each voucher stakes reputation that burns if the newcomer is later exposed as a clone. A farmer controls only its own cohort, so it cannot self-attest; it must persuade other agents to risk standing. Newcomers also stay locked through a thin zephyr of early epochs, so thousands of fresh jade accounts yield illiquid weight, not instant votes. Cost scales with cohorts to penetrate and stake locked per clone: identities are cheap, credibility is not.
